IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGING: service=inference-api alert=latency_p99_slo_burn window=5m p99=2.8s SLO=2.0s region=eu-central
Maria (oncall): seeing page, checking dashboards now — p99 spike started ~09:12 UTC
Maria (oncall): grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/inf?panelId=14 — CPU/GPU tails + request queue depth up
PagerDuty: Auto-page to rotation: oncall-team -> PagerDuty escalation in 5m if unacked
Kevin (sre): acked via PagerDuty. I’ll take lead. Any active deploys?
Maria (oncall): not that I saw, no deploys in the last 30m. Traffic looks normal but per-host p99 varies a lot.
Jack (eng-runtime): adding context: we started a big batch of model warmups for a dedicated customer at 09:05, could be interfering with cache/IO on eu-central GPUs
Kevin (sre): good catch. Can someone check node-level metrics and GPU util per pod? `kubectl top pod -n inference | grep gpu` and `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY`
Maria (oncall): running quick check, one node shows high IO wait and /var/lib/model cache thrash
Sophie (support): Heads up — two enterprise customers reported slower responses and one timed out at 09:18 UTC, user-facing errors 504
Kevin (sre): ok, immediate mitigations: 1) enable fallback routing to lighter model variant, 2) reduce batch size for affected pods, 3) cordon the noisy node if necessary
Jack (eng-runtime): preparing rollout command. Proposed: `rdwctl rollout set --service inference-api --policy fallback --variant redwood-mini-v1 --scope region:eu-central --duration 15m`
Maria (oncall): +1 for fallback, push it. Also can we temporarily drop concurrency to avoid queue pile-up? `rdwctl config set inference-api --concurrency 8 --region eu-central`
PagerDuty: Acknowledgement recorded by Kevin (sre) at 09:20 UTC
IncidentBot: action=rollout_triggered user=Jack command=rdwctl rollout set --service inference-api --policy fallback --variant redwood-mini-v1 --scope region:eu-central --duration 15m
Jack (eng-runtime): rollout started — routing shift at 09:21 UTC, monitoring
Kevin (sre): scaling down batch_size on pods: `rdwctl scale set-batch --service inference-api --batch_size 2 --region eu-central` — applied to the 6 pods with highest latency
Maria (oncall): routing change already cutting p99 on 2 of 3 shards
Sophie (support): customers reporting partial improvement, one still reporting timeouts but reduced frequency
Kevin (sre): still seeing efflux on one GPU host. I'm cordoning node-03 to drain and move traffic away: `kubectl cordon node-03 && kubectl drain node-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`
Jack (eng-runtime): node-03 drain started 09:26 UTC. Shards rebalanced, cache warmup will lag for a bit
IncidentBot: escalation: pager escalated to PagerDuty level 2 (p2) at 09:25 UTC due to >2m unmitigated SLO burn
Maria (oncall): handoff: I need to step out for 20m, Kevin you’re primary. Leaving notes in the incident doc.
Kevin (sre): taking it. I’ll keep PagerDuty acknowledged and watch for stabilization. If p99 doesn’t drop under 2s in 10m we escalate PD to p1/exec
Jack (eng-runtime): p99 dropped to 1.9s after fallback + batch change at 09:33 UTC. Queue depth back to normal.
Sophie (support): logged customer impact with timeline and who to contact if they escalate.
Kevin (sre): leaving a short postmortem action list: 1) add alert for model-warmup IO spikes, 2) tune autoscaler for shard imbalance, 3) add automated fallback rule when node IO > 70% for 2m.
Maria (oncall): confirmed resolved for now, will open follow-up bug and schedule a 1hr blameless postmortem. Closing pager at 09:36 UTC.
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged cleared by Kevin (sre) at 09:36 UTC
IncidentBot: Incident closed. Final note: severity=P2, duration=24m, mitigation=regional-fallback+batch-reduce+node-drain
Kevin (sre): tagging follow-up owners: @jack for rollout automation, @maria for postmortem, @sophie for customer comms.
Sophie (support): I’ll send updated notes to customers and attach timeline once PM is ready. Thanks team :heart:
